questions.question: What is the domain of a random variable $X\colon S\to\mathbb{R}$?
options: The real line $\mathbb{R}$, irrespective of the choice of sample space $S$
The sample space $S$
The set $[0,1]$
The event $X\le x$

questions.question: If $S=\{HH,HT,TH,TT\}$ and $X$ counts heads, what is $X(HT)$?
options: $HT$

questions.question: Besides being a function $X\colon S\to\mathbb{R}$, which condition does the definition of a random variable require?
options: $X$ is one-to-one, so different outcomes give different values
$\{X\le x\}$ is an event for every $x\in\mathbb{R}$
$X$ takes only finitely many different values
$X(\omega)\in[0,1]$ for every outcome $\omega\in S$

questions.question: Why is a random variable not the same object as an event?
options: It is always a subset of $S$.
It is a function on outcomes, while an event is a subset of the sample space.
It has no relationship to outcomes, while an event is built directly from outcomes.
It must have probability one.

questions.question: A die is rolled, with $S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$ and every subset of $S$ an event. Which of these is not a random variable on $S$?
options: $X(\omega)=\omega^2$
$X(\omega)=3$ for every $\omega\in S$
$X(\omega)=1$ if $\omega$ is even and $X(\omega)=0$ if $\omega$ is odd
$X(\omega)$ is the word even or odd, according to $\omega$

questions.question: For a random variable $X\colon S\to\mathbb{R}$ and a number $t$, what kind of set is $\{X\le t\}$?
options: The set of outcomes $\omega\in S$ with $X(\omega)\le t$
The single value $X(\omega)$ that is observed, if it is at most $t$
A set that cannot be specified until the outcome is observed
The interval $(-\infty,t]$ on the real line

questions.question: A die is rolled, with $S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$, and the only events are $\varnothing$, $\{1,2,3\}$, $\{4,5,6\}$ and $S$. Which function $X\colon S\to\mathbb{R}$ is a random variable for this collection of events?
options: $X(\omega)=\omega$, the face shown
$X(\omega)=1$ if $\omega$ is even and $X(\omega)=0$ if $\omega$ is odd
$X(\omega)=5$ if $\omega\le3$ and $X(\omega)=-2$ if $\omega\ge4$
$X(\omega)=\omega$ if $\omega\le3$ and $X(\omega)=7$ if $\omega\ge4$
